===== README.md =====
# Lucifer's Diary

A personal writing platform — a dark literary publication site for serious long-form writing.

This is a monorepo containing two packages:

- **`backend/`** — NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL API (port 3001)
- **`frontend/`** — Next.js App Router app — public reading site + admin panel (port 3000)

## Documentation

- [`docs/PROJECT.md`](docs/PROJECT.md) — complete build specification (architecture, data model, API routes, business rules)
- `Lucifer's Diary Design System/` — color tokens, typography, component specs, brand voice
- `lucife'r sdiary Hi-Fi design/` — interactive hi-fi mockups and original design brief

## Surfaces

- **Public site** (`/`) — readers browse stories and series, read them, and leave anonymous likes (no account required)
- **Admin panel** (`/admin`) — single-author authoring tool, JWT-protected by a shared password

## Tech stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend API | NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL |
| Frontend | Next.js (App Router) |
| Auth | Single admin password → JWT |
| Styling | CSS Modules + Tailwind (shadcn internals only) |
| UI Components | shadcn/ui |
| Animations | GSAP + ScrollTrigger |
| Animated Icons | AnimateUI |

## Running locally

```bash
# Backend (port 3001)
cd backend
npm install
npx prisma migrate dev
npm run start:dev

# Frontend (port 3000)
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

The public site is served at `http://localhost:3000`; the admin panel is at `http://localhost:3000/admin`.

## Deploying

End-to-end aaPanel runbook — Node.js + PM2 + Nginx + PostgreSQL — lives in [`DEPLOY.md`](DEPLOY.md).

Relevant moving parts:

- [`ecosystem.config.js`](ecosystem.config.js) — PM2 manifest. Boots both apps, runs `prisma migrate deploy` on the API.
- [`deploy/nginx.conf.example`](deploy/nginx.conf.example) — Nginx site config. Proxies `/api/*` to the backend, everything else to Next.js, with cache headers on `_next/static/`.
- [`backend/.env.example`](backend/.env.example) and [`frontend/.env.local.example`](frontend/.env.local.example) — env templates.
- `GET /api/health` — liveness probe (no DB call).
- `GET /api/health/ready` — readiness probe (round-trips Postgres).

===== DEPLOY.md =====
# Deploying Lucifer's Diary on aaPanel

End-to-end runbook for putting the site on an aaPanel VPS. Assumes
you already have a domain pointed at the server and Node.js + PM2 +
Nginx + PostgreSQL installed via aaPanel's app store.

## 1. Prepare the server

In aaPanel, install (one-time):

- **Node.js 20** (App Store → Node.js Version Manager → install 20)
- **PostgreSQL 16+** (App Store → PostgreSQL Manager)
- **PM2** (comes with Node.js Version Manager; or `npm i -g pm2`)
- **Nginx** (already installed on a fresh aaPanel)

Open a terminal (aaPanel sidebar → Terminal) and confirm:

```bash
node -v       # v20.x
npm -v
psql --version
pm2 -v
```

## 2. Create the database

In aaPanel → Databases → Add Database (PostgreSQL):

- Database name: `lucifer_diary`
- Username: `lucifer`
- Password: pick a long random string

Note the connection string — it'll be:

```
postgresql://lucifer:PASSWORD@localhost:5432/lucifer_diary
```

## 3. Pull the code

In aaPanel → Files, navigate to `/www/wwwroot/` and clone:

```bash
cd /www/wwwroot
git clone https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary.git luciferdiary
cd luciferdiary
```

(Use HTTPS + a personal access token if the repo is private.)

## 4. Configure environment variables

### Backend

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
nano backend/.env
```

Set:

- `DATABASE_URL` — the string from step 2
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD` — your admin login password
- `JWT_SECRET` — generate with `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('hex'))"`
- `PORT` — `3001` (matches the Nginx config)
- `FRONTEND_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN,https://www.YOUR_DOMAIN`

### Frontend

```bash
cp frontend/.env.local.example frontend/.env.local
nano frontend/.env.local
```

Set:

- `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN/api`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — `https://YOUR_DOMAIN` (no trailing slash)

> **NEXT_PUBLIC_\* values are inlined at build time** — re-run the
> frontend build after changing them.

## 5. Install + build

From the repo root:

```bash
# Backend
cd backend
npm ci
npx prisma migrate deploy        # applies every migration in order
npx prisma generate              # regenerate the client
npm run build                    # tsc -> dist/
npm run seed:tags                # OPTIONAL: seed the 591-tag taxonomy

# Frontend
cd ../frontend
npm ci
npm run build                    # produces .next/
```

## 6. Run with PM2

From the repo root:

```bash
pm2 start ecosystem.config.js
pm2 save                          # persist across reboots
pm2 startup systemd               # follow the printed `sudo` command

curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health
curl http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health/ready    # checks DB connectivity
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:3000/                 # Next homepage
```

## 7. Nginx reverse proxy

In aaPanel → Website → **Add Site** → enter your domain. After it
creates the site:

- Open the site's "Config File" tab
- Replace the contents with `deploy/nginx.conf.example` from this repo
- Replace `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `/www/wwwroot/luciferdiary/frontend` with
  your actual values
- Save and reload Nginx

In aaPanel → Website → SSL → **Apply for SSL** → Let's Encrypt. Tick
both `YOUR_DOMAIN` and `www.YOUR_DOMAIN`. aaPanel will rewrite the
config to listen on 443 and add the cert paths automatically — the
location rules from `nginx.conf.example` survive intact.

## 8. Smoke test

Visit `https://YOUR_DOMAIN`. You should see:

- The homepage with a sticky header (logo · search · controls)
- `/admin/login` lets you in with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
- `/api/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`
- `/sitemap.xml` lists every published URL
- `/feed.xml` validates as Atom

## 9. Updating

Each time you push a new commit:

```bash
cd /www/wwwroot/luciferdiary
git pull

# Backend
cd backend
npm ci                            # only re-runs install when the lockfile changed
npx prisma migrate deploy         # picks up any new migrations
npm run build                     # tsc -> dist/

# Frontend — `rebuild` wipes .next/ so old chunk hashes don't linger
cd ../frontend
npm ci
npm run rebuild

# Restart both
pm2 restart ecosystem.config.js
```

> **Cache note:** the CMS HTML is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`
> via `next.config.ts`, so admin pages always fetch fresh after a
> rebuild. Public pages keep their default revalidation behavior, and
> hashed chunks under `/_next/static/` stay `immutable`. If a writer
> still sees a blank CMS after deploy, hard-reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) once
> — the immutable chunks are fine to keep, only the stale HTML needs
> to clear.

## Troubleshooting

**`prisma migrate deploy` says no schema** — make sure you're inside
`backend/` when running it. The schema is at `backend/prisma/schema.prisma`.

**`502 Bad Gateway`** — PM2 isn't running, or it's crashed. Check
`pm2 logs lucifer-api --lines 100` and `pm2 logs lucifer-web --lines 100`.

**Admin login returns 401** — the `JWT_SECRET` in `.env` doesn't
match the one used to sign existing tokens. Clear localStorage in
your browser and log in again, or rotate to a fresh secret.

**`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` change doesn't take effect** — those are
baked in at build time. Re-run `npm run build` in `frontend/` after
editing `.env.local`, then `pm2 restart lucifer-web`.

**Hostname or DNS error from Prisma** — the database isn't reachable
from the API process. Try `psql "$DATABASE_URL"` with the same env;
fix the connection string until that succeeds.

**Migrations diverged on a fresh DB** — only run `prisma migrate
deploy`. Never run `prisma migrate dev` or `prisma db push` against
production; they can drop columns.

**Blank CMS / `ChunkLoadError` after deploy** — the browser is
holding onto cached HTML that references chunks the new build
deleted. The CMS is configured `Cache-Control: no-store` so this
should self-heal on next request, but if a tab was already open
during the rebuild, hard-reload it (Ctrl+Shift+R). To prevent it
entirely, use `npm run rebuild` (wipes `.next/` first) and
`pm2 restart lucifer-web` in that order.

# Lucifer's Diary — Design System

> A writing platform that feels like a literary journal read by lamplight.

Lucifer's Diary is a publication site for serious long-form writing. The aesthetic is a **dark literary magazine** — moody, unhurried, typographically confident. The darkness is warm and intimate, never aggressive or techy. Every design decision serves reading.

There are two surfaces:

1. **Public reading site** — homepage with sections of stories and series, individual story / chapter reading pages, series detail pages. This is where readers spend time.
2. **Admin panel** — desktop-only authoring tool. Sidebar layout, tables, forms. Shares the same dark theme but is utilitarian.

---

## Sources

This design system was built from a written design brief titled *"Design Overview — Writing Platform"*, supplied directly. There is **no attached codebase, Figma, or screenshot reference** — the brief is the source of truth. Every token, component spec, and interaction rule below traces back to it.

If/when an actual codebase exists, future iterations should pull from it (theme tokens, component implementations) rather than this document.

---

## Index

| File | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | This file — brand context, content + visual foundations, iconography |
| `SKILL.md` | Skill manifest for use as a Claude Code agent skill |
| `colors_and_type.css` | All CSS custom properties + base element styles |
| `fonts/` | Variable TTFs: Playfair Display, Lora, DM Sans (regular + italic) |
| `preview/` | Design-system tab cards (colors, type, spacing, components) |
| `ui_kits/public/` | Reading site UI kit — homepage, story page, series page |
| `ui_kits/admin/` | Admin UI kit — dashboard, table, post editor |
| `assets/` | Logos, icons, brand artifacts |

---

## Content Fundamentals

**Voice — quiet, confident, literary.** Copy on this site is written by people who care about prose. Headlines and section labels are short and unornamented; nothing winks at the reader. The tone is closer to a printed journal's masthead than to a SaaS dashboard.

**Casing.** Story and series titles are written in **Title Case** — they are *titles*, treated with respect. Section headings on the homepage (e.g. "Latest", "Series", "Author's Choice") are also Title Case. UI labels, nav, button text use **Sentence case** ("Start reading", "Save draft", "New chapter"). Tag pills and small structural labels use **UPPERCASE** with `letter-spacing: 0.06em` — small caps energy.

**Person.** The reader is addressed in second person where it occurs at all ("Continue reading", "Your reading list"), but most copy is impersonal — it describes the work, not the user. The author is referenced by name. The platform itself is rarely "we"; it tries to disappear.

**Density.** Sparse. Metadata under a story is *date · 7 min read · 124 likes* and nothing more. No taglines, no marketing strapline, no "Read this if you liked…" cross-sells. White space (well, dark space) is content.

**Specific examples.**

- Hero CTA: **Start reading** *(not "Begin your literary journey")*
- Empty state on a section: **No stories yet.** *(not "Looks like there's nothing here yet — check back soon!")*
- Save confirmation: **Saved.** *(green, 2.5s, then gone)*
- Delete confirmation: **Delete this chapter? This cannot be undone.** *(plain `window.confirm`)*
- Loading: **Loading…** *(muted, 14px, no spinner)*
- Like count, no number padding: **3 likes**, **127 likes**
- Author's Note label: **AUTHOR'S NOTE** *(uppercase, accent gold, then italic Lora body)*
- 404: **This page is not in the volume.**

**Emoji.** None. Ever. The brand voice is too literary for them. Unicode glyphs (`←` `→` `·` `⠿`) are used sparingly as functional ornaments — arrows in pagination, middle dots in metadata, the braille-six drag handle in admin.

**Punctuation.** Em dashes — generously. Middle dots `·` separate metadata fields. Curly quotes "like these" in body content where possible.

# Design Overview — Writing Platform

This document is the complete design brief for the public-facing frontend. Read it before writing any CSS or component code. The goal is a dark, literary aesthetic — the kind of website a serious writer would be proud to have their work published on.

---

## Aesthetic Direction

**Dark literary magazine.** Think a well-designed independent literary journal — moody, unhurried, typographically confident. The darkness is not aggressive or techy. It is warm and intimate, like reading by lamplight.

This is a site for reading. Every design decision should serve that purpose. Nothing should compete with the text.

What to avoid:
- Generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics
- Purple gradients
- Bright whites or stark contrasts
- Decorative elements that don't serve the content
- Anything that looks like a blogging template

Define all colors as CSS custom properties in `:root`.

  --bg:           #0A0908;   /* near-black with warm undertone */
  --bg-surface:   #121110;   /* card and panel backgrounds */
  --bg-raised:    #1A1816;   /* hover states, code blocks, raised elements */

}

The accent `#BF9B5E` is warm gold. Use it for:

- Part numbers on chapters
- Author's Note border and label
- Like button when liked (use a soft red `#e07b7b` instead for the heart)
- Active state on pagination
- The "Start reading" CTA button

43b1048 feat(t5): FLIP-based tag-filter reflow on /search, feature-flagged (#186) (#191)
Tag clicks on /search now glide the result grids from their old slots
to their new slots via GSAP Flip, instead of snapping after the server
navigation. Mirrors https://demos.gsap.com/demo/flexbox-filtering/.

Architecture (works across App Router server-side navigations, which
replace the DOM tree):
  1. TagBar's click handler snapshots Flip.getState on every
     [data-flip-grid] in the document BEFORE router.push.
  2. The snapshot lives in a module-level Map (frontend/lib/
     flipBridge.ts), keyed by the grid's flipKey + the destination
     tagIds. TTL = 1.5s — stale snapshots auto-purge.
  3. The new server render commits with a fresh React key on each
     CardGrid (filterKey = `${search}|${tagIds.sorted}`), forcing a
     remount. CardGrid's useGSAP mount-effect drains its snapshot
     by flipKey and runs Flip.from(state, {absolute:true, simple:true,
     onEnter, onLeave}).
  4. When a snapshot is consumed, CardGrid's scroll-triggered
     entrance reveal is skipped — Flip IS the entrance.

===== NOTES MIGRATION SQL =====
-- =====================================================================
-- Add multi-card, color-coded admin Notes — replaces the single
-- `notes` string column previously on `stories` and `chapters`.
--
-- Steps (must run in this order, single transaction):
--   1. Create the NoteColor enum.
--   2. Create the `notes` table + indexes + FK constraints.
--   3. Add the polymorphic-owner XOR CHECK constraint.
--   4. Backfill: one row per Story/Chapter that has non-empty
--      legacy notes content — title 'Note', color GOLD, orderIndex 0.
--   5. Drop the legacy `stories.notes` and `chapters.notes` columns.
--
-- Postgres 16 is required (gen_random_uuid() is built-in, no
-- pgcrypto extension needed).
-- =====================================================================

-- 1. Enum --------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TYPE "NoteColor" AS ENUM ('GOLD', 'CRIMSON', 'SAGE', 'INDIGO', 'AMBER', 'SLATE');

-- 2. Table + indexes ---------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE "notes" (
    "id"          TEXT        NOT NULL,
    "story_id"    TEXT,
    "chapter_id"  TEXT,
    "title"       TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "body"        TEXT        NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "color"       "NoteColor" NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GOLD',
    "order_index" INTEGER     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    "created_at"  TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    "updated_at"  TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL,

    CONSTRAINT "notes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);

CREATE INDEX "notes_story_id_order_index_idx"
    ON "notes" ("story_id", "order_index");
CREATE INDEX "notes_chapter_id_order_index_idx"
    ON "notes" ("chapter_id", "order_index");

ALTER TABLE "notes"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "notes_story_id_fkey"
    FOREIGN KEY ("story_id") REFERENCES "stories"("id")
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;

ALTER TABLE "notes"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "notes_chapter_id_fkey"
    FOREIGN KEY ("chapter_id") REFERENCES "chapters"("id")
    ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;

-- 3. Polymorphic owner — exactly one of (story_id, chapter_id) ---------
-- Prisma can't express this; enforced here so the invariant survives
-- any future code path that tries to write a row with neither or both.
ALTER TABLE "notes"
    ADD CONSTRAINT "notes_owner_xor"
    CHECK (("story_id" IS NULL) <> ("chapter_id" IS NULL));

-- 4. Backfill from legacy `notes` columns ------------------------------
INSERT INTO "notes"
    ("id", "story_id", "title", "body", "color", "order_index", "created_at", "updated_at")
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid()::text,
    "id",
    'Note',
    "notes",
    'GOLD',
    0,
    NOW(),
    NOW()
FROM "stories"
WHERE "notes" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM("notes") <> '';

INSERT INTO "notes"
    ("id", "chapter_id", "title", "body", "color", "order_index", "created_at", "updated_at")
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid()::text,
    "id",
    'Note',
    "notes",
    'GOLD',
    0,
    NOW(),
    NOW()
FROM "chapters"
WHERE "notes" IS NOT NULL AND TRIM("notes") <> '';

-- 5. Drop the legacy single-string note columns ------------------------
ALTER TABLE "stories"  DROP COLUMN "notes";
ALTER TABLE "chapters" DROP COLUMN "notes";

## 7. Repository, Docs & Prod↔Staging Code Delta

### Project overview

**Lucifer's Diary** is a single-author dark-literary writing/publishing platform — a CMS + public reader site for serious long-form fiction (stories and multi-chapter series), styled like "a literary journal read by lamplight." It is a **monorepo** (despite `docs/PROJECT.md` originally specifying two separate repos) with `backend/` (NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL) and `frontend/` (Next.js 16 App Router). There are exactly **two user types**:

- **Public readers** — no accounts. Browse stories/series, read, and leave **anonymous** likes/saves/reading-positions, identified by a UUID in browser localStorage.
- **Single admin/author** — JWT-protected by one shared `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, authors and publishes all content via `/admin`.

Tech stack: NestJS 11 + Prisma 6 + PostgreSQL (search via tsvector), Next.js 16 App Router, CSS Modules + Tailwind (shadcn internals only), GSAP/ScrollTrigger animations, TipTap rich-text editor, argon2 password hashing, `@nestjs/throttler` rate-limiting.

### Repo identity & root-folder inventory

- Remote: `git@github.com:Taha-Mahmoodi/lucifers-diary.git` (confirmed on both deploys).
- **`README.md`** (2,258 B) — monorepo overview, surfaces (`/` public, `/admin`), tech-stack table, local-run and deploy pointers, health probes (`GET /api/health`, `/api/health/ready`). License: "Private — all rights reserved."
- **`DEPLOY.md`** (6,152 B) — full aaPanel runbook: DB creation, env config (`DATABASE_URL`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET`, `PORT`, `FRONTEND_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`), `npm ci` + `prisma migrate deploy` + builds, PM2 (`ecosystem.config.js`), Nginx reverse proxy, SSL, and a 9-step **manual** update procedure (`git pull` → rebuild → `pm2 restart`). Notable warning: never run `prisma migrate dev`/`db push` against prod (can drop columns).
- **`docs/`** (3 files): `PROJECT.md` (41 KB — the complete build spec: architecture, full data model, every API route, business rules); `tag_taxonomy_3_tiers.md` (16 KB — a 3-tier erotica/romance tag taxonomy: Tier 1 default-visible, Tier 2 behind 18+ toggle, Tier 3 behind extreme-content opt-in — this is adult fiction); `tag_extras.json` (3.5 KB — extra tags with `isAdult` flags). DEPLOY references a "591-tag taxonomy" seed.
- **`Lucifer's Diary Design System/`** — a Claude Code **agent skill** (has `SKILL.md` with `name: lucifers-diary-design`). Contains `README.md` (12.7 KB brand/voice/visual spec), `colors_and_type.css` (CSS tokens), `fonts/` (Playfair Display, Lora, DM Sans variable TTFs), `preview/` (~22 design-system preview HTML cards), `ui_kits/public` + `ui_kits/admin` (the admin kit dir is **empty**). Hard brand rules: no emoji, no drop shadows, no gradients, accent gold `#BF9B5E` only for specific elements, text `#EDE8DE` never pure white.
- **`lucife'r sdiary Hi-Fi design/`** (note the typo'd folder name) — original hi-fi mockups: standalone React JSX (`Homepage.jsx`, `StoryPage.jsx`, `SeriesPage.jsx`, `AgeGate.jsx`, `components.jsx`, `tweaks-panel.jsx`), `data.js`, a `ds/` token copy, and `uploads/` with the source `DESIGN.md` brief (11 KB) + PNG/JPG mockup screenshots. This is the design source-of-truth the Design System was derived from.
- **`icons/SVG/`** — a single file, `Spycy icon.svg` (1.4 KB). Essentially a stub/placeholder folder.
- **`deploy/`** — `nginx.conf.example` (proxies `/api/*`→backend, rest→Next, cache headers on `_next/static/`).
- **`ecosystem.config.js`** — PM2 manifest, 2 fork-mode apps (`lucifer-api` runs `prisma migrate deploy && node dist/main.js`; `lucifer-web` runs `npm run start`), each `max_memory_restart: 512M`.

### Branch topology & deploy mapping

| Deploy | Path | Local branch | HEAD | Tracks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PRODUCTION** | `/www/wwwroot/Lucifersdiary/lucifers-diary` | `main` | **`6dd9633`** "fix(home): hero latest entries use series" (#176) | `origin/main` |
| **STAGING** | `/www/wwwroot/lucifersdiary-staging/lucifers-diary` | `develop` | **`43b1048`** "feat(t5): FLIP-based tag-filter reflow" (#191) | `origin/develop` |

Both working trees are **clean** (`git status` empty) and **exactly in sync** with their tracked remotes (`0 0` ahead/behind) — what's deployed equals what's committed, no local drift. The origin has ~22 remote branches (mostly merged `feat/*` and `fix/*` PR branches). The staging repo only has `develop` checked out locally (no local `main`), so the delta was computed against `origin/main`.

### PROD vs STAGING code delta — concrete feature list

`merge-base(origin/main, develop) == 6dd9633` (= prod HEAD). **Staging is a strict, clean fast-forward ahead of prod: 10 commits ahead, 0 behind.** Prod has nothing staging lacks. `git diff --stat origin/main..develop`: **53 files changed, +2,661 / −436**.

The 10 commits, by theme:

**A. Multi-card color-coded admin Notes (5 commits, #177–#181)** — the biggest feature. Replaces the legacy single `notes String?` column on Story/Chapter with a proper **`Note` model** (polymorphic owner storyId XOR chapterId, `title`, `body`, `NoteColor` enum [GOLD/CRIMSON/SAGE/INDIGO/AMBER/SLATE], `orderIndex`).
- `#177` backend: new `Note` model + `NoteColor` enum, new `src/notes/` module (admin-only CRUD: `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/notes`), and migration `20260608200000_add_notes_model` that creates the enum/table/indexes/FKs, a DB-level `notes_owner_xor` CHECK constraint, **backfills** legacy note strings into the new table, then **DROPs `stories.notes` and `chapters.notes`**. DTOs now 400 on a `notes` field (`forbidNonWhitelisted`).
- `#178` frontend: replaces slide-out `NotesDrawer` with a persistent right-column `NotesPanel` + `NoteCard` (pill↔expanded) + `EditorWithNotes` 2-col wrapper; per-note debounced autosave; deletes orphaned `NotesDrawer.*`.
- `#179`/`#180`/`#181` notes UI polish: panel grows horizontally (`clamp(360px,32vw,600px)`) and to full viewport height when a note is open; sticky-top fix; micro-interactions (per-note color glow, fade-ins, reduced-motion handling).

> **Deployment risk / ordering hazard:** migration `#177` drops columns after backfill. The commit message explicitly warns the **old frontend must NOT be deployed against this backend alone** — backend + frontend must ship together. Because this migration runs automatically via `prisma migrate deploy` in `ecosystem.config.js` on API boot, promoting `develop`→`main` and restarting prod will irreversibly drop `stories.notes`/`chapters.notes` on the **production** DB (`lucifer_diary`). This is the single most important thing to flag before any prod promotion.

**B. GSAP animation suite "T1–T5" (5 commits, #182–#191)** — a set of micro-interaction features, each in its own commit:
- `#187` **T4 — smooth scroll restore** (`useReadingPosition.ts`): returning readers glide back to saved reading position via GSAP ScrollToPlugin instead of jumping; guards against wasted PATCH writes during the programmatic scroll, respects reduced-motion. (Builds on the existing anonymous reading-position feature.)
- `#188` **T3 — physics click feedback** (new `lib/pressFeedback.ts`): CustomBounce squish + color flash on Like/Save/Share/QuoteShare, plus a Physics2D confetti burst on Like. Adds a `@property --press-flash` registration in `globals.css`.
- `#189` **T2 — FLIP pill↔NoteCard morph**: GSAP Flip morph between collapsed/expanded note states (depends on the Notes panel above).
- `#190` **T1 — macOS-dock magnetic hover** (new `lib/useMagneticDock.ts`): cursor-proximity scale/lift across card rows (search, browse, hero, continue-reading, chapter list); bails on reduced-motion and coarse-pointer devices.
- `#191` **T5 — FLIP tag-filter reflow** on `/search` (new `lib/flipBridge.ts`): result grids glide between filter states across App Router server navigations. **Feature-flagged OFF** via `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLIP_TAG_FILTER` — shipped disabled so even after promotion it stays inert until the env var is set.

New frontend libs landing on staging: `flipBridge.ts`, `pressFeedback.ts`, `useMagneticDock.ts`, plus expanded `gsap.ts` (registers Flip, ScrollToPlugin, Physics2DPlugin, CustomBounce, CustomEase) and a reworked `useReadingPosition.ts`.

### CI/CD, hooks, lint/test

- **No `.github/` directory → no GitHub Actions / CI workflows.** No `.gitlab-ci`, CircleCI, Travis, or Jenkins config either.
- **No `.husky/` directory → no git hooks.** No root `package.json` (so no monorepo-level lint-staged/pre-commit orchestration).
- **Deployment is entirely manual** per DEPLOY.md §9 (`git pull` → `npm ci` → `prisma migrate deploy` → `npm run build`/`rebuild` → `pm2 restart`). No automated pipeline; promotion of develop→main and prod deploy are hand-run by an operator.
- **Lint:** ESLint configured per-app (`backend/eslint.config.mjs`, `frontend/eslint.config.mjs`); backend also has `.prettierrc`. Backend `lint` script auto-fixes; frontend has bare `eslint`.
- **Tests configured but none written:** backend `package.json` defines `test`/`test:watch`/`test:cov`/`test:e2e` (jest), but **0 `.spec.ts`/`.test.ts` files exist** in `backend/src`, and **0 test files** in the frontend. Test infrastructure is scaffolded but unused — a notable gap given no CI gate either.

### .gitignore highlights (not committed)

Standard and sensible: `node_modules/`, build output (`dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, `out/`), **all env files** (`.env`, `.env.local`, `*.production.local`), logs, IDE dirs, `coverage/`, `.DS_Store`. Project-specific: `_reference/` and `mnt/` (pre-build snippets), `.claude/worktrees/`, `.pm2/`, and notably **`ecosystem.production.js`** (a prod-specific PM2 variant is git-ignored — implies env-specific overrides live only on the box, not in git). `backend/prisma/migrations/dev.db*` ignored but the real migration `.sql` files are committed.

### Tech-debt markers

- **Zero `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK`/`XXX`** across `backend/src`, `frontend/{app,components,lib}` on both prod and staging — code is clean of inline debt markers (commit messages instead carry explicit "Out of scope" / "future work" notes, e.g. drag-to-reorder notes and `/tag/[slug]` Flip support are deferred).
- Real tech-debt signals are structural, not marker-based: (1) **no tests despite jest scaffolding + no CI** to catch regressions on a manual-deploy flow; (2) the empty `Lucifer's Diary Design System/ui_kits/admin/` and stub `icons/SVG/` folders; (3) the typo'd `lucife'r sdiary Hi-Fi design/` folder name (apostrophe + spaces in a path is fragile for scripts/SSH); (4) `docs/PROJECT.md` is stale on one architectural point — it states "Two separate repositories. No monorepo," but the project is in fact a single monorepo (as README correctly describes).

**Bottom line:** Staging (`develop` @ `43b1048`) is cleanly 10 commits ahead of production (`main` @ `6dd9633`) with no divergence. The pending promotion bundles one schema-breaking feature (multi-card Notes, which **drops two prod columns** via an auto-running migration and requires coupled backend+frontend deploy) plus five additive GSAP animation features (T1–T5), one of which (T5 tag-filter reflow) ships behind an env flag and stays off until explicitly enabled.
